messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: INC-2026 rate-limiter-prod quota-anomaly (service=rate-limiter-prod) — 98% error rate on 502/429s detected across region=us-west-2. Auto-escalation in 5m if not acked.
pagerduty: INC-2026 -> PagerDuty page to @erin and @leo.
erin: Acked. I'm oncall. pulling metrics now. can someone check if limiter instances are healthy?
sam: looking at Grafana -> high qps on tenant_xyz and a sudden drop in limiter instance count around 13:27 UTC. CPU fine, but connection errors from limiter to quota-mapper.
jin: got logs tailing limiter pods: ``ERROR quota_lookup: rpc failed: context deadline exceeded`` repeated. also saw `config_service: reload succeeded` at 13:26:45 then spike.
erin: that reload timestamp matches timeline. did we push a quota-mapper config earlier? amanda, did you ship the rollout?
amanda: pushed a small quota-mapper rollout at 13:25 to roll out stricter tenant mappings (PR #3982). It targeted canary but looks like the config propagated to prod via config-service global refresh.
ops-runbot: runbook step 01 executed by erin: validate limiter health -> `kubectl get pods -l app=rate-limiter -n prod`
erin: pods show 5/8 ready across nodes, several restarts. starting `kubectl logs` on the failing pod: ``panic: runtime error: invalid memory address`` — but stack shows quota client timeouts first.
sam: quick mitigation idea: flip fallback to soft-quota (route to permissive path) to avoid 429s while we rollback config. can we toggle feature flag?
leo: @erin I can take the rollback if you want to coordinate. I'll also be the escalation owner if PD escalates.
erin: please do. amanda, what's the simplest rollback? is it reverting the config push or disabling refresh?
amanda: I can revert the mapping change in config-service and trigger a refresh. rollback PR already ready.
jin: while that's happening, we should also flip route fallback. Command: ``curl -XPOST https://ops-api.prod/features/limit-fallback -d '{"state":"on","scope":"global"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'`` — toggles to permissive fallback.
erin: running fallback toggle now.
erin: ``> curl ...`` response: `{"status":"ok","feature":"limit-fallback","state":"on"}`
sam: traffic shows 429 rate dropping from 42% -> 8% in 40s. latencies normalizing. good sign.
pagerduty: INC-2026 acknowledged by erin at 13:31 UTC. auto-escalation canceled.
amanda: rolling back config-service change now (PR revert merged). triggering config-service refresh.
ops-runbot: runbook step 03 executed: ``kubectl rollout undo deployment/config-service -n prod`` by amanda.
jin: config-service logs show refresh broadcast at 13:32:10, quota-mapper now reporting success on lookups. limiter clients stop seeing RPC timeouts.
leo: monitoring: errors continue to decline, error rate at 1.2% now. checking customer impact - any major customers?
sam: tenant_xyz was the top offender (testing load), but we saw a spike in real-customer traffic for partner-abc between 13:26-13:33. their requests largely returned 200 after fallback.
erin: I'm going to message CS to flag partner-abc about transient errors, but short-lived. Jin, can you keep an eye on pod restarts?
jin: pod restarts stopped after rollback, restarts are stable for 10m. heap traces from earlier look like nil pointer from config edge-case during hot-reload. filing bug.
amanda: filing follow-up: I'll add stricter canary constraints to prevent global refresh bleed in next deploy. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/PR/3990
leo: good. I'll follow up with post-incident notes. For now, mark as mitigated. anyone object to me resolving PD?
erin: go ahead. thanks team. great quick ops. :thumbsup:
pagerduty: INC-2026 resolved by leo at 13:40 UTC.
incident-bot: Incident summary: mitigation -> feature-flag fallback enabled (13:30 UTC), config rollback (13:32 UTC). Impact -> transient 429s/502s for ~7 minutes, highest affected tenants: tenant_xyz, partner-abc. Root cause -> global config-service refresh applied a canary mapping hotfix prematurely, causing quota-mapper RPC timeouts and subsequent limiter errors. Next steps -> (1) enforce stricter canary gating on config refresh, (2) add circuit-breaker for quota-mapper RPC failures, (3) postmortem doc by leo (due EOD).
leo: I'll draft the postmortem and link alert graphs + timestamps. erin, can you add the runbook updates for config-service safe-refresh?
erin: will do. adding runbook checklist items now.
jin: created issue for quota-mapper NPE and hot-reload safety: https://issues.internal/RED-5123
leo: thanks. closing thread.
